newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares jump on better results.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares jump on better results.

text.p: Nigeria's stock market on Thursday made one of its biggest one-day gains, closing 123.45 points higher on improved corporate results, traders said.
The all-share index soared to 6461.45 from Wednesday's 6,338.00. Turnover was 1,067,159 million from 2,590,215 shares.
Traders said the improved trading results and positive perception of leading equities were responsible for the jump.
Shares of Cadbury and AIICO insurance were among top finishers on their improved half-year results, they said.

Cadbury's after-tax profit rose to 180.6 million naira in the first six months of 1996 from 151.1 million naira in the same period in 1995, causing impressed traders to hike its price by 47 kobo to 25.00 naira.
AIICO also added 10 kobo to 6.00 naira as its after-tax profit for the six-month period rose to 20 million naira, nearly doubling the previous year's 11.5 million naira.

Delta Glass posted a markedly improved half-year net profit, hitting 91.8 million naira from 41.6 million naira in 1995, but the large quantity of its shares on the trading floor did not enable it to enjoy a price gain, traders said.

The results received enthusiastic welcome in view of the harsh operating environment. "Any company showing an improvement over last year's result should be commended," analyst Tunde Ayeni, at CSL Stockbrokers told Reuters.

Blue chip stocks remained in high demand, causing them to close higher. PZ Industries was 50 kobo up on Thursday, finishing at 35.20 naira while oil marketers Unipetrol and Total each rose 30 kobo to 37.30 naira and 44.80 naira, respectively.
National Oil was also 30 kobo up at 29.00 naira.
Nigerian Bottling Company closed at 27.50 naira, up 25 kobo and construction firm G. Cappa added 20 kobo to 6.85 naira.

Cement shares finished well up on the second day running, led by Benue Cement's 21 kobo rise to 4.46 naira. Ashaka Cement went 15 kobo higher at 15.95 naira while Cement Company of Northern Nigeria finished five kobo up at 2.65 naira.
But Afribank, whose recent rights issue was listed on Wednesday, slid 20 kobo to 6.00 naira as investors took profit.
Newly listed Guaranty Trust Bank was 15 kobo higher on sustained demand to 12.50 naira.
Guinness shares slumped by five kobo to 9.15 naira, further indicating tough times ahead for brewers.
The improved result by Delta Glass put an end to its fall on Thursday, closing at 6.14 naira.
But French trading conglomerate CFAO continued its free fall, losing nine kobo at 4.60 naira.
